Consult Summary:
- 39-year-old woman with 3-day history of severe diarrhea, vomiting, fever, and abdominal pain, not improving with oral rehydration salts; infectious gastroenteritis suspected.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe diarrhea ("very loose," initially watery) for 3 days, associated with vomiting and subjective fever.
- Onset: Diarrhea began 3 days ago; vomiting ongoing, last episode ~2 hours before consult.
- Frequency: Patient lost count but reported at least 4 episodes of diarrhea today; vomiting after every ingestion, including fluids.
- Associated symptoms: Severe abdominal pain centered around the navel (sore to touch, pain coincides with urge to defecate), subjective high fever ("literally boiling"/"roasting to touch").
- Other symptoms: No rash. No blood in stool or urine. No prior similar episodes. Normal baseline bowel habits (once daily, no prior diarrhea or constipation).
- Review of systems: No reported rash, blood in stool or urine, or urinary issues.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: None specified. No identified dietary triggers or recent travel.
- Epidemiological link: Brother and multiple people at his school with similar symptoms; recent contact with brother.
- Hydration: Able to urinate (last time ~1 hour ago), no comment on urine color.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- No prior abdominal problems or surgery.
- Occasional menstrual cramps (takes ibuprofen as needed).

Medications:
- Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented)—taken daily.
- Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented)—occasionally for menstrual cramps.
- Oral rehydration salts (homemade salt-sugar mix)—taken three times daily for past two days.
- Allergies: Not mentioned.

Social History:
- Occupation: Graphics designer.
- Living situation: Lives with mother and brother.
- Smoking: Denies smoking.
- Alcohol: Drinks a pint occasionally.
- Recreational drugs: Denies use.
- Diet: Describes as normal.
- Recent work impact: Unable to attend workplace; working from home due to illness.

Family History:
- Brother has similar symptoms (diarrhea and vomiting).

Physical Examination:
- No examination or vital signs documented.

Investigations:
- None performed yet.
- Planned: Stool sample to be collected and sent for analysis.

Assessment & Plan:

- Issue 1: Acute Gastroenteritis (likely infectious, possibly viral, but bacterial cause to be ruled out)
  - Infectious gastroenteritis suspected due to history and epidemiological link.
  - Advise ongoing oral rehydration with small, frequent sips.
  - Advised to continue using oral rehydration salts.
  - Light diet recommended (simple foods such as toast or biscuits); avoid fruits, vegetables, and milk products.
  - Urgent clinical appointment to check hydration status and send stool sample for analysis.
  - Advised to seek urgent/emergency care if symptoms worsen (especially if unable to keep down fluids or evidence of dehydration).

- General Plan:
  - Support for booking urgent clinic appointment.
  - Advised to call back or seek A&E attention if deterioration occurs.

Quality checks (document_quality):

● Missing but clinically expected elements: 
  - Medication allergies not asked/documented.
  - Objective physical findings and vital signs not obtained.
  - Complete medication reconciliation (other regular or recent medications not documented).
  - No urine color description.
● Internal conflicts from transcript: 
  - None identified.
● Transcript quality: 
  - Generally clear. Occasional minor hesitations, all relevant clinical information extractable.
